candidate.title: Inscriptions of Kambuja: Prasat Pram Loven inscription of Gunavarman
candidate.venue: Asiatic Society Monograph Series (archive.org full text)
candidate.ask_addressed: Southeast Asia: transmission of Sanskrit, Hindu-Buddhist religion and Indian scripts (Pallava-derived) to Funan, Champa, Java, Cambodia. Primary: Vo Canh inscription, Kutai Yupa inscriptions, Angkor-period Sanskrit inscriptions (Cœdès, Finot, Majumdar translations), Chinese envoy accounts (Kang Tai and Zhu Ying on Funan in the Liang shu or Nan Qi shu).
candidate.quote: The two kings Jayavarman and Rudravarman were rulers of Fu-nan in the last quarter of the fifth and the first half of the sixth century
candidate.summary: Majumdar summarises a twelve-verse Sanskrit stele (metres Vasantatilaka, Sloka, Sardulavikridita) with an invocation to Buddha, then Rudravarman and a Brahmin treasurer appointed by his father Jayavarman: Funan Sanskrit court verse with Buddhist and Brahmin elements.
candidate.limits: Fragmentary text; summary only. OCR of the lines on the Brahmin treasurer is corrupted and not quoted.

strand.what: Sanskrit court poetry in Buddhist-invocation inscription

text.work: Prasat Pram Loven inscription of Gunavarman

composition.basis: Majumdar: Jayavarman and Rudravarman reigned in the last quarter of the 5th and first half of the 6th century; Briggs (opened) gives Rudravarman's reign from 514

text.witness: Stone stele from Thup Muoi, Plain of Reeds (Vietnam); Cœdès' edition (BEFEO 31, p. 1)

reason: metadata_mismatch: the quoted passage and summary (invocation to Buddha, Rudravarman, Brahmin treasurer, six verses) are from Majumdar no. 3, the Ta Prohm inscription of Rudravarman, not no. 2 Prasat Pram Loven of Gunavarman (12 verses, consecration of a Visnu footprint, no Buddha invocation), which is what title, work, locator, verse count and witness describe. Quote is on the page but under a different work; resubmit as no. 3 with a corrected strand.
